messages:
jamie: Heads-up — customer 'AcmePayments' (private VPC) saw a p95 token latency jump after the kernel-selector tweak this morning. I have a profile dump and some histograms.
priya: Ugh. Can you paste the p50/p95/p99 numbers and which model + sequence lengths?
ajmie: (typo) jamie: p50=18ms, p95=220ms, p99=780ms for ~1k seq samples. Model: redwood-compat/llama2-70b-quant, seq distribution: 32/128/512 with 512 being ~12% of requests.
alex: I pulled a flamegraph from the VPC agent — looks like a lot of time in `kv_cache::lookup` and then a fallback path into `cpu_attention::kernel_exec` for some shards. Link: https://internal.graf.redwood/flame/1830012345 (view-perm:eng-runtime)
priya: That fallback to CPU kernel would absolutely explode p99. Did the kernel selector choose a new vendor kernel or a different tiling heuristic in the canary?
jamie: We rolled kernel-selector v2.3.1 last night (auto-tiling heuristics + topology-aware host assignment). Canary on 10% of traffic, turned to 100% at 02:12 UTC. Deploy-bot notes: "canary -> prod promotion by priya at 02:12"
deploy-bot: [deploy] canary promoted: kernel-selector v2.3.1 by priya at 2026-02-14T02:12:03Z
maria: For private VPCs we also saw the agent library fallback because the GPU driver on one host didn't expose the expected cuBLAS kernel symbol. That triggers CPU fallback in our runtime. We need to detect and emit a metric when the vendor kernel is unavailable.
alex: Agreed. Proposed new metrics: `redwood_kernel_selector_decisions{kernel="cuda_fused",outcome="ok"}` and `redwood_kernel_selector_decisions{kernel="fallback_cpu",outcome="miss"}` plus `redwood_kv_cache_hits_total` / `redwood_kv_cache_misses_total`. Also token-level breakdowns: `redwood_token_latency_ms_bucket` with labels route/model/route_id and components: `queue_ms`, `kv_lookup_ms`, `compute_ms`, `kernel_switch_ms`.
jamie: Sample token breakdown from the VPC profile: queue_ms=5ms, kv_lookup_ms=140ms (lots of misses + remote kvcalls), compute_ms=60ms, kernel_switch_ms=15ms. That kv_lookup is the killer.
priya: Is kv lookup remote for private deployments? I thought we pinned KV cache to local host for VPC agents. If it's remote something is wrong with our placement or the prefix cache warmup didn't run.
maria: For this customer the KV warmup cron failed (airgap mirror sync didn't push the prefetch blobs). So initial requests do remote fetches to objectstore via the VPN->edge forwarder which added 120ms per token. We should have an alert when kvcache_hit_rate drops below 85% over 5m.
ajmie: jamie: ok let's add those alerts. Also proposal for air-gapped metrics export: run a small forwarder in the customer's VPC that scrapes local runtime metrics and serves them on a HTTPS endpoint (mutual TLS) that the customer's Prometheus/Grafana scrapers can pull. For more locked-down customers, support a push path that writes securely to an S3 bucket inside the VPC which their infra team scrapes.
alex: Implementation notes — two approaches:
1) Pull-mode: our forwarder exposes `/metrics` with basic auth + mTLS; customer Prometheus uses file_sd or static scrape target. This keeps data inside their network.
2) Push-mode (airgap): runtime writes periodic snapshots to a signed file on a shared volume (or s3 compatible endpoint). Customer runs a small importer that converts snapshots into a Prometheus TSDB scrapeable format.
priya: For security we need mTLS cert rotation & audit logs. Also the forwarder should redact any PII tags (route ids that contain customer tokens). Add a config option `metrics_label_whitelist`.
maria: On dashboards — add a per-route panel with stacked bars: queue / kv_lookup / compute / kernel_switch with p50/p95 lines and a heatmap for kernel selector outcomes. Example alert: if `rate(redwood_kernel_selector_decisions{outcome="fallback_cpu"}[5m]) > 0.05` then page SRE.
ajmie: Also saw a regression after we enabled multi-tiling for 512 sequences — compute improved for long seqs but selector started preferring a vendor kernel that is incompatible with older drivers in some private clusters. We should add a canary that runs a compatibility probe against the kernel symbol table on host start and emit `redwood_kernel_compat_ok{host}`.
alex: I'll prepare a small PR that: (a) emits the new metrics, (b) adds the kvcache hit-rate alert, (c) adds kernel compatibility probe. Will also include a Grafana dashboard JSON for export.
priya: Thanks — can you include a short scrape_config snippet for private VPC docs?
alex: sure — snippet: ```scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'redwood-vpc-runtime'
    scheme: https
    tls_config:
      ca_file: /etc/ssl/redwood/ca.pem
      cert_file: /etc/ssl/redwood/client.pem
      key_file: /etc/ssl/redwood/client.key
      insecure_skip_verify: false
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['10.0.5.23:9100']
    metrics_path: /metrics
    bearer_token_file: /etc/prometheus/redwood-token```
maria: Perfect. Can we also add a lightweight exporter mode that aggregates per-route KPIs into one timeseries per route to avoid cardinality explosion for very chatty customers? Suggest `redwood_route_kpi{route_id=...,kpi="p95_token_ms"}` and similar.
jamie: Good call. Ok action items: alex -> PR with metrics + dashboard + alerts (ETA 48h). maria -> coordinate with customer infra re: forwarder deployment & certs. priya -> rollback policy added to canary docs in case of kernel incompat. I'll open a short runbook.
priya: I'll also schedule a short postmortem with AcmePayments support thread and include a timeline.
ajmie: jamie: thanks all. If PR lands before EOD let's run a small canary in the affected VPC (20%) and validate kv warmup + kernel probe before full promotion. :thumbsup:
